newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Erica Rossler to buy Bulgaria clothing firm.
newsitem.headline: Erica Rossler to buy Bulgaria clothing firm.

text.p: Germany's ready-made clothes firm Erica Rossler has shown interest in buying 80 percent of Bulgaria's clothing factory Boryana by mid-April and plans to produce models under the trade mark of Pierre Cardin.

"We have received a letter by the industry ministry, saying that a privatisation procedure has been opened for the firm on February 12 and the buyer was Germany's company Erica Rossler," Boryana's director Miroslav Makaveev told Reuters on Friday.
The price of the deal and the way of payment are yet to be decided, Makaveev added.
The privatisation deal is expected to be finalised between the end of March and mid-April, he added.
Makaveev said Erica Rossler had won recently a tender for a production of ready-made clothes under the trade mark of Pierre Cardin and some of the models were expected to be produced in Bulgaria.

"There is an agreement that Boryana will be included in the Erica Rossler's production programme for Pierre Cardin clothes and in August we are expected to start the production of two or three models," he said.
The Boryana firm, situated in Bulgaria's northern town of Cherven Bryag, was established in 1968.

Its 1996 turnover was some one million marks and more than 90 percent of its output has been exported to western countries, mainly to Germany and Italy, Makaveev said. The company has no bad debts, he added.
Erica Rossler has pledged to invest 800,000 German marks by the end of this year to renew its ageing equipment.

Bulgaria, which badly needs income from privatisation to meet huge foreign debt payments, completed 509 privatisation deals in 1996 worth 95.93 billion levs and said it was planning to concentrate on fewer, higher-value deals in 1997.
